sources.quote: in 1171, he abolished the weak and unpopular Shiʿi Fāṭimid caliphate
Although he remained for a time theoretically a vassal of Nūr al-Dīn, that relationship ended with the Syrian emir’s death in 1174.
at length in June 1171 sent him a formal order to do so, at the same time notifying the 'Abbasid caliph himself of his action. The order was obeyed
Then, on September 13, al-'Ādid had died, and no successor was named.
Whatever further plans he may have had in view were cut short by his death on May 15, 1174.

description.en: Egypt plus Damascus and southern Syria, taken from 1174 as Saladin united the Muslim territories around the Crusader states.
description.ar: مصر مع دمشق وجنوب سوريا، أُخذت من 1174 حين وحّد صلاح الدين الأراضي الإسلامية حول الدويلات الصليبية.
description.he: מצרים בתוספת דמשק ודרום סוריה, שנלקחו מ-1174 כאשר צלאח א-דין איחד את השטחים המוסלמיים סביב מדינות הצלבנים.

sources.quote: from 1174 until 1186 he zealously pursued a goal of uniting, under his own standard, all the Muslim territories of Syria, northern Mesopotamia, Palestine, and Egypt.
Although he remained for a time theoretically a vassal of Nūr al-Dīn, that relationship ended with the Syrian emir’s death in 1174.
Whatever further plans he may have had in view were cut short by his death on May 15, 1174.
on an urgent appeal from the commandant at Damascus occupied it, almost without opposition, on October 28, 1174.

description.en: After Hattin: 'Most of Palestine was once again Muslim'. Interior Palestine, Transjordan (Kerak 1188) and southern Syria under Ayyubid princes; from 1191-92 the coast from Jaffa north was Frankish again, and Jerusalem/Bethlehem with a corridor (and Nazareth) were Frankish 1229-1244.
description.ar: بعد حطين: 'Most of Palestine was once again Muslim' [أصبحت معظم فلسطين مسلمة مرة أخرى]. فلسطين الداخلية وشرق الأردن (الكرك 1188) وجنوب سوريا تحت أمراء أيوبيين؛ ومن 1191–92 عاد الساحل من يافا شمالًا فرنجيًا، وكانت القدس/بيت لحم مع ممر (والناصرة) فرنجية في 1229–1244.
description.he: לאחר חיטין: “Most of Palestine was once again Muslim” [רוב פלשתינה שוב הייתה מוסלמית]. פנים פלשתינה, עבר הירדן (כרך 1188) ודרום סוריה תחת נסיכים איובים; מ-1191–92 היה החוף מיפו צפונה שוב פרנקי, וירושלים/בית לחם עם מסדרון (ונצרת) היו פרנקיות ב-1229–1244.

sources.quote: On July 4, 1187, six days after the capture of Tiberias, he dealt the Crusaders a crushing blow at the decisive Battle of Ḥaṭṭīn (Ḥiṭṭīn). Most of Palestine was once again Muslim.
Le Krak du Désert, a heavily fortified Crusader citadel, was built on the site of the ancient fortress in 1132; it fell to the Muslims in 1188
on September 2, 1192, the two signed a three-year peace treaty. The coast from Jaffa north remained in Christian hands, but Ascalon was to be restored to Saladin
Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and a corridor running to the sea were ceded to the kingdom of Jerusalem.
a 10-year treaty that temporarily restored Jerusalem, Nazareth, and Bethlehem to the Christians. In 1244, however, the Ayyubid sultan al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb definitively restored Jerusalem to Islam.
Safed passed from hand to hand during the Crusades until captured by Baybars I, who razed its citadel (1266).
Saladin delayed only a day to secure the capitulation of Tiberias (July 5) before marching toward Acre.
all the major ports south of Tripoli, with the exception of Tyre, were in Moslem hands. These included Beirut, Jaffa, Ascalon, and Sidon
hunger finally forced the heroic garrison of Kerak to capitulate. Al-Malik al-'Ādil received the message from the nearly starved garrison and gave them free egress (November 1188).

On Saladin's death (March 4, 1193) the unity imposed by his personality and authority was disrupted, and all the provinces (except that of Kerak) became in effect separate and independent principalities.
On September 2, a truce for three years was signed by the representatives of the king and the sultan. The Christians were to hold a narrow strip along the coast from Tyre to Jaffa.
The murder of Tūrān-Shāh, which ended Aiyūbid rule in Egypt, left a void that had to be filled quickly by the men who had created it.

notes.en: Partial coastal units: Ayyubid 1187-1191, Frankish afterwards. Internal division among Ayyubid princes not mapped. Upper and Lower Galilee partial because parts (e.g. Safad, Nazareth) were Frankish again in the 1240s.
notes.ar: وحدات ساحلية جزئية: أيوبية 1187-1191، وفرنجية بعد ذلك. لم يُرسم التقسيم الداخلي بين الأمراء الأيوبيين. الجليل الأعلى والأدنى جزئيان لأن أجزاء منهما (مثل صفد والناصرة) عادت فرنجية في أربعينيات القرن 13.
notes.he: יחידות חוף חלקיות: איובי 1187-1191, פרנקי לאחר מכן. החלוקה הפנימית בין נסיכים איוביים לא מופתה. הגליל העליון והתחתון חלקיים משום שחלקים מהם (למשל צפת ונצרת) היו שוב פרנקיים בשנות ה-1240.

description.en: Syrian Ayyubid principalities only (Egypt and Sinai now Mamluk), until the Mongol invasion of 1260.
description.ar: الإمارات الأيوبية السورية فقط (أصبحت مصر وسيناء الآن مملوكية)، حتى الغزو المغولي عام 1260.
description.he: הנסיכויות האיוביות הסוריות בלבד (מצרים וסיני כבר ממלוכיות), עד הפלישה המונגולית ב-1260.

sources.quote: The Ayyubid decline in Egypt was completed with the Mamluk accession to power following the battle at Al-Manṣūrah (1250), but the dynasty persisted in some areas of Syria until 1260
When the Mongol cataclysm of 658/1260 destroyed the Syrian Ayyubid kingdom of al-Nāṣer, the Mamluk regime was able to occupy his former dominions.
a treaty was concluded (April 1253) between Aybeg and an-Nasir, by which the former would hold Egypt and a slice of Palestine at the banks of the Jordan, including Jerusalem as well as the coastline
in 1260 the Mongols invaded Syria, sacked Aleppo, frightened Damascus into subjection, and destroyed the Aiyūbid principalities of Syria and Palestine.
In September of 1260, at 'Ain Jālūt, the Mamluks crushed Kitbogha, and occupied almost all of Syria.

notes.en: How southern Palestine was divided between the Syrian Ayyubids and Mamluk Egypt in 1250-1260 was not verified; the Mongols briefly held much of the area in 1260 (see ilkhanate).
notes.ar: لم يُتحقق من كيفية تقسيم جنوب فلسطين بين الأيوبيين في الشام ومصر المملوكية في 1250-1260؛ وسيطر المغول لفترة وجيزة على معظم المنطقة عام 1260 (انظر ilkhanate).
notes.he: לא אומת כיצד חולקה דרום פלשתינה בין האיובים בסוריה לבין מצרים הממלוכית ב-1250-1260; המונגולים החזיקו לזמן קצר ברוב האזור ב-1260 (ראו ilkhanate).
